LESSON: PRESENTATION SKILLS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.5: Presentation skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Presentation skills. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate tonal variation, articulation and sequencing of activities for each day of the week stress to express self confidently

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. use appropriate tonal variation, articulation and sequencing of activities for each day of the week stress to express self confidently
   In simple words: practise until you can use appropriate tonal variation, articulation and sequencing of activities for each day of the week stress to express self confidently. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Presentation skills using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Presentation skills in the examples.
2. Explain Presentation skills to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Presentation skills.
4. Show that you can: use appropriate tonal variation, articulation and sequencing of activities for each day of the week stress to express self confidently

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Presentation skills using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Presentation skills important for a Grade 1 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

2. Learners attempt to respond to questions related to variation, articulation and sequencing of activities for each day of the week stress to express self (before, after, then) confidently
3. Learners sing songs, rhymes and recite poems c) appreciate the use of related to routine activities transition words to
4. Using familiar and unfamiliar

SECTION: REMEMBER
